title: MOXIR 17.10 — three versions of the rig: minimal, middle, full
status: PROPOSAL for the owner's look. Same hall, same DJ booth, same zones as the base rig; what changes is how much is hung and how it is used. Nothing here is checked against the venue, a load calculation or the rental house.
owner: 2026-09-28, on /moxir: "make 3 version with the full, midle, and simple minimalistic and also look to moxir mood, set, vibe and its the undegroudn rave thing lights like that not the commercial shit"

method.what: Each version is a complete rig file generated from the base (scripts/place/rigs/moxir-2026-10-17.json) by scripts/rigbuild/versions.mjs: the base's stage, truss, night, photometry and opening, this file's groups, effects, budget and looks. The three files are committed beside the base and checked current by a test.
method.practice: The underground rules below are the design brief. Where a source was opened and says it, it is cited (sources); where no citable source was found in this session they are marked 'design hypothesis' — scene practice widely repeated but not documented by a source we could open (web search budget exhausted 2026-09-28; owed: RA In Residence: Bassiani 2017-02-01, RA 'Tbilisi and the politics of raving' 2016-08-15, Vice 'Is This Georgian Club the New Berghain?' 2017-06-16 — confirmed to exist, not read).

rules.rule: Darkness is a material: most of the room is unlit most of the time; a look says where light is NOT (levels 0).
The building is the set: its structure revealed in pieces (a column, the press, the roof frame), never floodlit or decorated.
Strobes are the peak: violent white hits against the industrial fabric, then dark again.
Heavy haze, so a beam reads as a column of the architecture rather than a spot on the floor.
One colour at a time, and few of them: cold white, deep red, a warm amber (the blinders' tungsten-like white); never rainbow chases.
Light from low and from behind: the DJ in silhouette, not in a key light.
Stillness and slow sweeps, then a hit: the looks are held states, the movement is between them.
None of the commercial vocabulary: no CO2 jets, cold sparks, confetti or butterfly effects.
rules.status: design hypothesis — the owner's own words ('not the commercial shit') are the brief

ATMOSFERA.what: Pietro Leonardi, 'The role of light design in Nightclubs', Atmosfera Mag (undated; opened 2026-09-28): "The Berghain floor remains mostly dark, mirroring the intense and relentless techno played within"; on warehouse raves, "strobe lights creating intense visual contrasts against the industrial backdrops"

MIXMAG-2018.what: Duncan Dick, 'The art of club design', Mixmag, 31 Aug 2018 (opened 2026-09-28). Simeon Aldred (Printworks London): "The key to a 'found' space is not to change it drastically, but to amplify what is already there." "Make it safe for the audience, but then leave it alone."

DAZED-2016.what: Dazed, 'Lightning strikes Berghain but party rages on', 30-31 Aug 2016 (opened by the research agent 2026-09-28): the emergency lights coming on described as 'blinding bright' — bright light as the exception

versions.title: Minimal — the cut, simple: fixed lights only
versions.summary: No stage, no towers: the DJ stand alone, the crane parked over it. THE CUT — one straight 12 m line sloped 15° under the bridge, low house left, high over the press — on 3 bridled hoists with tie-offs, lit ONLY by what the rental house has that does not move: a curtain of 7 COB200 straight down, an X of 6 PL5403 crossing over the DJ, 4 red PL5403 grazing the bridge; 6 PL5403 pillars at the column bases, 8 red column uplights, 3 on the press; 2 hazers. No moving heads, no strobes.

haloTruss.why: Option 6 of the ten truss versions, built as a comparison beside option 4 on Minimal. The triangle is the object; the lamps live on it.
haloTruss.section_class: 290 mm square box truss (Global Truss F34; Prolyte H30V is the same class)
haloTruss.corner: Global Truss F34 C20 2-way corner 60° (F34C20: 8.80 kg, outer 1000 x 1000 x 290 mm)
haloTruss.corner_source: https://globaltruss.de/en/F34-2-way-corner-C20-600/F34C20 (opened 2026-09-29): "F34 2-way corner C20 60° … Weight: 8,80 kg … Dimensions (L/W/H): 1000 x 1000 x 290 mm". A 60° corner is a STANDARD catalogue part of the 290 mm system (the same series lists C19 45°, C21 90°, C22 120°, C23 135°).
haloTruss.corner_leg_why: The page gives the C20's outer box, not its leg on the centre line. 0.5 m is ASSUMED so a side = 0.5 + 3 m F34300 + 0.5 = 4.0 m node to node; read the real leg from Global Truss's 'DWG files (F34 System)' on the same page before ordering (a longer leg makes the side longer — stock straights only).
haloTruss.orientation: Apex toward the crowd (+z), base edge behind the DJ under the bridge's back girder.
haloTruss.orientation_why: (1) The base edge lies behind the DJ and 0.3 m clear of the press in plan (its truss z 3.50-3.79; the press ends at z 3.2), so nothing hangs over the machine; with the apex toward the press, the triangle's point would sit 0.25 m off the press's left edge and a side would cross over its corner. (2) From the floor the apex points at the people and the two long sides run back to frame the DJ against the press — the halo reads as an arrowhead opening onto the performer. (3) Either way one corner lies beyond the bridge (the triangle is 3.46 m deep, the two girders span 2.9 m face to face); the apex is one pick, the base would be two.

craneX.pieces_why: each arm = a 2 m straight + the junction's 1 m + a 2 m straight: 4 straights and one 4-way flat cross junction for the whole X

junction.code: Global Truss F34 SQ-4133 '4-way cross junction'
junction.across_basis: legs 0.5 m from the centre — ESTIMATE: the maker's page gives the weight, not the leg length; the rental house's own junction may differ (then the straights change, not the X)

craneX.section_class: 290 mm square box truss (Global Truss F34 — src/rigbuild/pieces.js; Prolyte H30V is the same class but does not couple to F34: one system for the whole X)
craneX.trim_why: the shortest drop the rigging allows at the girder bottom the hall model carries (8.15 m, rail 7.6 m): a 90° bridle's apex hangs half its span under the flange — 1.1 m for the bridge-arm picks whose legs reach both girders (2.2 m apart) — then the climbing hoist's hook-to-suspension-plate minimum (≈0.50 m, read from the Chainmaster D8Plus 500 kg dimension sheet, p. 6) and ≈0.10 m of shackles: top chord 8.15 − 1.1 − 0.5 − 0.1 = 6.45 m, bottom chord 6.16 → 6.15 m. The crane rail is DISPUTED (6.6–8.4 m): at the low end every height here drops by 1.0 m (bottom chord ≈5.15 m, under the press crown 5.6 m, 0.1 m clear of it in plan) — measure the girder bottom on site before the trim is set.

motion.pendulum_L_basis: from the bridle anchors on the girder flange (8.15 m) to the hung mass's centre (the truss, 6.15–6.44 m, plus lamps standing 0.2–0.6 m above the top chord): 1.5–1.9 m. T = 2π√(L/g), g 9.81 m/s².
motion.restraint: each pick is a two-leg V bridle (the bridge-arm picks' V spans across the bridge, z; the crowd-arm picks' V spans along it, x), so the rigid X cannot translate either way without stretching a leg; two restraint steels at every arm end, up to the girders and spread in plan, stop it turning. What is left is the give of wire and slings: small, not zero.
rules: no pan or tilt move over the full range faster than 4 s (the heads' reaction torque is what pushes a hung truss)
no periodic movement (a chase, a sweep back and forth) with a period between 1.7 and 4 s — 0.7× to 1.5× the pendulum's 2.5–2.8 s — the band where a small push each cycle builds up
cue fades that move heads on the X are at least 4 s in the show's cue list
the crane locked out and isolated for the whole event (it is the rig's structure)

picks.bridle: two legs, one to a beam clamp on each girder's bottom flange (2.2 m apart), 90° between the legs, apex 1.1 m under the flange
right under a girder: two legs to beam clamps on that girder's flange 1.5 m apart along it, 90° between the legs, apex 0.75 m under the flange

tieoffs.what: at every arm end, two restraint steels up to beam clamps on the girders, spread in plan: the bridge arm's ends to both girders (a V across the bridge), the crowd and back ends to their own girder 1.5 m either side (a V along it). To the crane, not the floor: the crowd end hangs over people, where a floor anchor is a trip and crush point; the nave columns (≈11 m off) are the fallback for the bridge arm's ends.

movingFixtures.rule: no fixture that pans, tilts, rotates or zooms by motor is mounted above 0.6 m (its mounting face); no ground mover's beam passes through the dance zone below 2.5 m in any look; the two lasers are fixed, and every laser beam stays >= 3 m over any floor a person can stand on.

gs-one-shaft.title: Blackout + one shaft
gs-one-shaft.intent: Black. One thin white shaft stands straight up from behind the press into the roof, the DJ a silhouette cut out of it. Nothing else.

gs-columns-below.title: Columns from below
gs-columns-below.intent: The eight column faces glow cold white from their feet and fade to black before the roof; a low white beam at the foot of each far column. The floor is dark, the structure stands up out of it.

gs-roof-reveal.title: Roof reveal
gs-roof-reveal.intent: The space-frame roof appears in pieces: the beams behind the press fan open into the trusswork, then the column beams stand up beside them; a dim white graze along the crane bridge above. Still, no sweep.

gs-slow-fan.title: Slow fan
gs-slow-fan.intent: The column beams lean slowly in across the nave, the wall beams lean slowly out toward the side walls, the booth beams open into a wide fan up into the roof. The move is the slow crossfade in from the reveal (6 s); nothing flashes.

gs-cross-beams.title: Cross beams
gs-cross-beams.intent: Beams from both walls lean in and cross high over the dance floor, above head height, like a lattice in the haze. The booth beams stay upright and dim behind.

gs-red-room.title: Red room
gs-red-room.intent: Deep red only and low: the columns and the press glow red from their feet, a dim red graze on the crane bridge, the booth beams stand still and dim. The DJ is a dark shape against the red press. The roof stays black.

gs-white-cathedral.title: White cathedral
gs-white-cathedral.intent: The whole nave in cold white: every column beam straight up in mirrored pairs, the wall beams up the walls, the crane bridge grazed white from the cut above, a narrow fan behind the DJ, who stands as a silhouette against the lit press.

gs-blinder-hit.title: Blinder hit
gs-blinder-hit.intent: One hard white blinder hit on the front of the floor from the cut, cut in from black and cut back to black. The COB curtain is held steady by the look; the room flashes only by the cue cutting in and out. STROBE-CAPABLE: lights the blinder, held steady, cut by the cue; flash rate never above 3/s.

gs-haze-wall.title: Haze wall
gs-haze-wall.intent: Haze rolls from behind the DJ; all seven booth beams stand straight up in a row, a wall of light in the haze behind the silhouette; the rest is dark. EFFECT: hazers on (hazer-back, hazer-hall) — NOT SIMULATED.

gs-spark-hit.title: Spark hit
gs-spark-hit.intent: From black: the booth beams open in a narrow white fan and back-light one burst of cold sparks rising in the pit in front of the silhouette; then black. (The sparks are not drawn in the room.) EFFECT: cold spark machines in the pit, one burst on the cue — NOT SIMULATED, plume height and clearance UNVALIDATED (maker manual owed).

gs-laser-roof.title: Laser into the roof
gs-laser-roof.intent: OPTIONAL, NOT IN THE LOOP. In the dark, red laser lines from the top of the cut into the roof frame, one dim red shaft behind the DJ. Needs a certified laser safety officer before it is ever switched on. LASER: off by default; requiresLaserSignOff: written at level 0, the laser stays dark until a human raises it after a certified laser safety officer signs off (Class 4, owed).

Crane height approximate and strobe rates assumed (Gevorg 2026-10-01: correct later); charts for the rest owed.

k-doors.title: Doors
k-doors.intent: Before the first act: haze up, the nave columns barely glowing amber from their feet, the press a dim silhouette. Enough to find your way, nothing that performs.

k-the-x.title: The X
k-the-x.intent: The X of PARs on the cut lights the DJ from above while the column beams cross the nave in an X high over the floor — the rig drawing its own sign.

k-tunnel.title: Tunnel
k-tunnel.intent: The ten column beams lean hard in from both walls and meet in a pointed arch high over the dance floor: a tunnel of white in the haze, the crowd underneath it.

k-green-core.title: Green core
k-green-core.intent: MOXIR's green, once: every nave column glows green from its foot and the press goes green behind the DJ, while a narrow white fan stands up behind the booth. The only colour in the night that is the brand's.

k-amber-dust.title: Amber dust
k-amber-dust.intent: The teaser's warm sodium light: amber up the columns and under the crane bridge, low, like dust in a factory afternoon. No beams. A breath between the white sections.

k-lights-up.title: Lights up
k-lights-up.intent: The end of the night: every column and the crane bridge in warm white at full, all beams off. Clean-out light, not a show look.

k-blade.title: The blade
k-blade.intent: The curtain at full white under the cut: in haze a sheet of cold white whose top edge is the cut's 15° slope; the four bridge PARs red at 60 % draw the crane as a frame. Nothing else.

k-hit.title: The hit
k-hit.intent: From black: the curtain and the six X PARs at full white together. No strobe channel (rates are untested on the PL5403) — the hit is the cue's own 0 s cut in and out.

k-one-shaft.title: One shaft on the DJ
k-one-shaft.intent: Black. The centre curtain PAR alone, full white, straight down on the DJ: one hard shaft from the cut, the DJ in it. Nothing else.

k-cathedral-x.title: White cathedral + the X
k-cathedral-x.intent: White cathedral with the X of PARs on the cut drawn over the DJ.

k-fan-hit.title: Fan hit
k-fan-hit.intent: From black, the seven booth beams open in a narrow white fan straight up behind the DJ. No sparks (no chart); the cue cuts in at 0 s.

candidates.realLightsWhy: EVERY lamp is a real light (Emily 2026-10-01: 'i want 100% ident what we will have, you can optimize'): the room is the night as it will be, no picked few, no baked stand-ins. Measured on PONYO (RTX laptop, 1440x900): 40-52 fps; with shadows on the 12 lamps putting the most light in (shadowCasting.js shadowLampCap) 36-49 fps. A phone will not hold this: the 8-lamp budget is the fallback.
candidates.looksWhy: The set's own looks were made for the hung rig; on the ground versions they sit beside ground looks of the same name ("White cathedral", "Red room"), which the Touch page could not tell apart (Emily 2026-10-01: rename, keep both).

par-columns.note: one on each nave column's inner face and one on its back face, grid lines around the dance floor and the stage — minus the two BACK faces at the far end (z 48, one each side) that the curtain's 7 PARs take from the order of 50.
